WEDDING DAY TIMELINE BUILDER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

A minute-by-minute wedding day timeline, with the sunset worked out

Enter your date, city and ceremony time and get the whole day in order: hair and makeup start times, the first look and portraits, the ceremony, cocktail hour, dinner, toasts and dancing, back-timed from the hour the music has to stop. A sunset portrait slot is placed at golden hour without moving anything else, and a ceremony time advisor tells you which start times work best. Print a separate sheet for the photographer, DJ and caterer.

Planning photos? Read how long wedding photos take, with worked times.

1. The day

Pick a city close to the venue, or choose "Other" to type coordinates. Sunset is computed from the date and place; it is accurate to a few minutes. If the music stops after midnight, enter the clock time (for example 00:30).

2. Photos and getting ready

3. The reception

Enter the date, city, ceremony time and end time, then click Build.

Your timeline

TimeWhat happensNotes

When each vendor should arrive

Arrive byWho

Which ceremony start time works best?

StartScoreWhy

Every half hour from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM is rebuilt with your other answers and scored: the program must fit before the music stops, an outdoor ceremony should end well before sunset, the sunset portraits need a free slot, and the cocktail hour should not stretch while guests wait.

How it is built

Back-timing: the day is worked backwards from the ceremony (guests seated 30 minutes before, family, wedding party and couple portraits and a first look before that, then the dress, then hair and makeup) and forwards from it (photos or cocktail hour, entrance, first dance, dinner, toasts, cake). Open dancing is whatever time is left before the music stops, and the page tells you when that is too little.

Sunset: computed from the date, latitude and longitude with the NOAA solar position formulas. The sunset portrait session is 15 minutes starting about 30 minutes before sunset. It is an overlay on the couple's free time, so no other event moves; if every nearby slot is taken the page says which event is in the way.

Rules of thumb: the durations (15 minutes for a first look, 3 minutes per family group, 90 and 60 minutes for hair and makeup, 4 minutes per toast) are common planning conventions, not measurements. Change any of them above, and confirm every time with your vendors and venue.

Checked: the test suite compares computed sunsets with published almanac values, builds timelines across cities, seasons and start times, and confirms that events stay in order, the couple is never double-booked and the program ends at the time you set.

Common questions

How long should wedding photos take?

Allow about 15 minutes for a first look, 30 for portraits of the two of you, roughly 10 minutes plus 2 per person for the wedding party, and about 3 minutes per family group plus a few minutes of setup. For a party of 8 and 10 family groups that is about 1 hour 45 minutes in total, which is why many couples do a first look and move most of it ahead of the ceremony.

Do we need a first look?

No, but without one every portrait happens after the ceremony and eats into the cocktail hour. This builder shows both versions: with no first look it tells you how many minutes the cocktail hour stretches while guests wait, so you can decide with real numbers.

What time should sunset portraits happen?

Aim to start about 30 minutes before sunset and keep it to 15 minutes, so the light is low and warm but you still have it. The builder works out sunset for your date and city and places a 15-minute session at the nearest time that does not collide with anything the two of you must attend.

What time should our ceremony start?

Late enough that the ceremony and family portraits are in good light, early enough that the ceremony ends well before sunset if it is outdoors, and with enough room before the music stops for dinner, toasts and an hour or more of dancing. The ceremony time advisor scores every half hour from 10 AM to 7:30 PM against your own details and shows the best three.

How much time do we need for hair and makeup?

About 90 minutes for the bride or lead client and about 60 for each other person is a common starting point. The builder splits the list across your artists, shows each person's start and finish and works the start time backwards from when the dress goes on.

Is my wedding information uploaded anywhere?

No. Everything is calculated in your browser, nothing is sent to a server and there are no accounts. Use Save timeline to keep a file you can load again, and print or export the timeline for each vendor.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you enter, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere, so use Save timeline and keep the file.

Everything runs in your browser. Your dates, names and choices are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (timeline_built, example_loaded, ics_downloaded, csv_downloaded, text_copied, file_saved, sheet_printed) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.

How long wedding photos take, with a worked timeline

The photo plan decides the shape of the whole day. Portraits are the only part of a wedding that can happen before the ceremony or after it, and where they go decides when hair and makeup starts, how long guests wait at the cocktail hour, and whether there is light left for sunset pictures.

Build your own timeline for free

How long each block takes

Common planning conventions, which you can change in the builder: a first look is 15 minutes, portraits of the two of you 30, the wedding party 10 minutes plus 2 per person, and family portraits about 3 minutes per group plus 5 minutes of setup. For a party of 8 and 10 family groups that is 15 + 30 + 26 + 35 = 106 minutes, or about 1 hour 45 minutes.

One wedding, two plans

A Saturday in mid October in Charleston, South Carolina, ceremony at 4:30 PM, music stopping at 10:30 PM, 120 guests, a one-hour cocktail hour and five people getting hair and makeup with two artists. Sunset is at 6:46 PM.

MomentWith a first lookWithout
Hair and makeup begins10:44 AM12:30 PM
First look2:24 PMnone
Family portraits begin3:35 PM5:00 PM
Ceremony4:30 PM4:30 PM
Couple joins the cocktail hour5:10 PM6:36 PM
Cocktail hour length for guests1 h1 h 46 min
Grand entrance6:00 PM6:46 PM

With a first look, everything is done before the ceremony and the cocktail hour is the hour it was meant to be. Without one, the same portraits start at the end of the ceremony, the couple reaches the cocktail hour at 6:36 PM and guests wait an extra 46 minutes, and the sunset portraits compete with the entrance and the first dance for the same minutes. The other fix is a longer cocktail hour planned on purpose, with food and a bar to match.

Where sunset portraits fit

The builder places a 15-minute session about 30 minutes before sunset. In the first-look plan that is 5:41 PM, in the middle of the cocktail hour, so no guest-facing event moves. It treats the ceremony, portraits, entrance, first dance, dinner and toasts as times the couple must be present and looks for the nearest gap.
